messages.text: Kane becomes first English winner of Ballon d'Or in 25 years

metadata.summary: Harry Kane has become the first English winner of the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after being honoured at a ceremony in London.
metadata.content: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker becomes first English winner of award in 25 years | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker becomes first English winner of award in 25 years Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or at London ceremony; Bayern Munich striker becomes first English winner of award in 25 years; England captain hit 73 goals for club and country last season; ex-Tottenham forward beat Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal to prize Tuesday 27 October 2026 00:07, UK Image: Kane was the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or in 25 years Harry Kane has become the first English winner of the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after being honoured at a ceremony in London. Michael Owen was the last player from England to receive the prestigious individual accolade in 2001, but Kane's incredible 73-goal haul last season for club and country earned him the award from French magazine France Football. Bayern Munich forward Kane was a popular winner in the capital and has followed in the footsteps of Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen as a Ballon d'Or winner from England. metadata.summary: From forgettable EFL loan spells to being crowned the best player in the world, it is no wonder Harry Kane’s former boss thinks of his Ballon d'Or win as a fairy tale.
metadata.content: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker completes 'Cinderella story' from EFL loans to world's best player | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker completes 'Cinderella story' from EFL loans to world's best player Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or to become first Englishman to land award in 25 years; Bayern Munich and England captain's Ballon d'Or victory called 'Cinderella story' by Tim Sherwood; watch Bayern vs Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, kick-off 5.30pm Declan Olley Football Journalist @declanolley Monday 26 October 2026 23:50, UK From forgettable EFL loan spells to being crowned the best player in the world, it is no wonder Harry Kane’s former boss thinks of his Ballon d'Or win as a fairy tale. "This is a Cinderella story we've never seen before," ex-Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood, who gave Kane his full Premier League debut, tells Sky Sports . "He keeps breaking records, and I keep thinking, 'Are we talking about the same kid?' "There was always a chance, because he felt like there was no ceiling - he would always just break through and go further. "I mean, not even Harry would say he could believe it, I would suggest." metadata.summary: Jacob Fearnley retired with an injury after losing 5-1 in the first set against Arthur Fery to give his fellow countryman a place in the second round at the Vienna Open.

Fearnley was broken by Fery in just his second service game, with the British No 1 winning the next two games on the bounce and looking set to consign his opponent to a comprehensive first-set loss. Fearnley, though, then put a stop to the contest, shaking the umpire's hand and retiring with an unspecified injury, allowing Fery safe passage to the next stage of the competition. metadata.summary: London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas claimed a record-equalling third women's Ballon d'Or.
metadata.content: Alexia Putellas wins Ballon d'Or: How the Women's Super League has benefitted from the midfielder's immense influence | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Alexia Putellas wins Ballon d'Or: How the Women's Super League has benefitted from the midfielder's immense influence London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas wins 2026 Women's Ballon d'Or for record-equalling third time; Putellas captained Barcelona to quadruple last season; watch London City Lionesses vs Man City Women on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Premier League, kick-off 12pm Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Monday 26 October 2026 23:34, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexia Putellas makes WSL history after winning Ballon d'Or. London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas claimed a record-equalling third women's Ballon d'Or. The Spain international captained Barcelona to a quadruple last season, including Champions League glory, as she scored 26 goals and provided 15 assists for club and country. The 32-year-old then sensationally joined London City Lionesses in one of the biggest transfers in WSL history. Since her move in July, Putellas has scored three goals and has an assist in her seven WSL games.
